title: Canonical completed coefficient, slice tower and localized scalar interfaces
statement:
Define the following canonical interfaces, keeping all site object, morphism, coefficient and derived-localization universes independent as allowed by [def-weil-size-convention]. For a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and its recorded uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and any scheme $T$, let $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(R/t^n)_T$ be the recorded completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Define the completed scalar section of $a\in R$ by the constant section $a$, constant-sheaf sheafification, and the canonical constant-to-completion map. For any scheme $W$ and any object $U\to W$ of its small pro-etale site, define coefficient restriction of commutative ring sheaves as sectionwise restriction along $V\mapsto(V\to U\to W)$, equivalently restriction to the slice followed by the recorded identification with $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No finite-type condition is imposed on $T$, $W$ or $U$.

For a site $(\mathcal C,J)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], a ring sheaf $O$, its ordinary module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and an object $U\in\mathcal C$, define restriction on strict $\mathbf N^{\mathrm{op}}$-towers by applying the ordinary slice restriction termwise. If this restriction is additive and exact and the indicated unbounded derived categories exist [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], define derived tower restriction by its exact induced derived functor. Define the strict-limit complex of a cochain complex of strict towers by degreewise ordinary inverse limit, the restriction/strict-limit comparison by degreewise $\mathrm{limit.post}$, and its $n$th cochain projection by the degreewise ordinary limit projection. Defining the comparison requires additivity of ordinary restriction; no claim that it is invertible or computes a total derived limit is made here.

Finally, for a commutative ring sheaf $O$ on such a site, a commutative ring $A$ and a ring map $a:A\to\Gamma(O)$ into compatible global sections, define the induced $A$-linear structure on the ordinary unbounded derived category of $O$-modules by restricting the global-section scalar action on module Homs and then passing to the derived category. For $s\in A$, define the canonical ring map $A[1/s]\to\Gamma(O[1/a(s)])$ by the localization lift of $A\xrightarrow{a}\Gamma(O)\to\Gamma(O[1/a(s)])$, using the actual sheafified sectionwise localization and its unit [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. All these definitions are transparent re-exports of the existing constructions; they assert none of the separate exact-localization, slice-comparison or lisse-image theorems.

Package the normalized strict-derived-limit interfaces as the following predicates, not existence theorems. A strict-limit realization for a specified functor L from the unbounded derived category of strict towers to the derived module category, with a specified cochain comparison η from the strict-limit complex followed by Q to Q followed by L, consists of countable products in the target, a levelwise evaluation functor ev normalized by an isomorphism on complexes, and product/projection and boundary maps making L(Z) the recorded derived-limit triangle [def-weil-derived-limit] of ev(Z). On every K-injective strict tower complex I, η_I is invertible and the nth component of its product map is η_I inverse, followed by Q of the ordinary nth limit projection and then the specified evaluation identification. Slice-limit compatibility for a ring sheaf O and a chart U consists of additive exact ordinary restriction, exact levelwise tower restriction, specified total right derived limits L and L_U with universal units η and η_U invertible on K-injective towers, strict-limit realizations as just specified on both sites, and a natural isomorphism L followed by derived slice restriction to derived tower restriction followed by L_U. On every complex its composite with the tower derived-factorization comparison is the derived ordinary-restriction factorization comparison, followed by Q of the strict-limit comparison, followed by η_U. On K-injective towers the same isomorphism intertwines each nth limit projection using the two inverse units and the ordinary and tower derived-factorization comparisons. Use the recorded adic coefficient category size conventions [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and the canonical sheafification, local-equivalence, smallness and standard derived-category instances on the pro-etale site and its literal slices; these introduce no additional assumptions or alternative objects.
